items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Clear names (encryptWriter, decryptReader, getEncryptor, validateSource), a package doc describing the stream format, and doc comments on exported functions. Minor nit: the handler_test import block is not grouped the gofmt way ("errors" sits next to the encryption import).

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Crypto is split cleanly into config.go and encryption.go, and functions are short (flush, Close, next, LoadKey). The closer-order logic in storageReadWriteCloser is clear. Minor: getEncryptor calls Validate and then LoadKey, which runs validateSource again.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Chunk length is bounds-checked (minChunkLen/maxChunkLen), EOF becomes ErrUnexpectedEOF, the key is copied, the HMAC is compared with hmac.Equal, errors stick in ew.err/dr.err, and constants are named. Errors are wrapped with %w and ErrInvalidKey. No errors are swallowed in production code.

items.name: Interface changes limited to the specified ones
items.name_zh: 接口变更仅限题目要求
items.evidence: The mandated changes are done, callers are updated, and unencrypted output is unchanged. But storage.PathGenerator keeps its old signature and hardcodes `EnsureFileName(filename, gzip, false, unique)`, so the backends can never add .enc. This works around the backends instead of updating them, against the repo convention.
